faqs.a: Range = fuel in the tank (litres) x mileage (km per litre). With 12 litres at 15 km/L, range = 12 x 15 = 180 km.
Your real mileage comes from experience: fill the tank, note the odometer, drive normally, refill, and divide the kilometres driven by the litres added. Do this over 2–3 tanks for a reliable average.
faqs.q: How do I find my vehicle's real mileage?

faqs.a: Fill needed = tank capacity - current fuel. Cost = fill needed x price per litre. With a 40 L tank, 12 L inside, and fuel at 100 per litre: (40 - 12) x 100 = 2,800.

fuel-range-calculator.formula:
Current range (km) = current fuel (L) x mileage (km/L)
Full-tank range (km) = tank capacity (L) x mileage (km/L)
Fuel to fill (L) = tank capacity - current fuel
Fill cost = fuel to fill x price per litre
Fuel level (%) = (current fuel / tank capacity) x 100

fuel-range-calculator.workedExample: A car has a 40-litre tank with 12 litres inside, mileage of 15 km/L, and fuel priced at 100 per litre. Current range = 12 x 15 = 180 km. Full-tank range = 40 x 15 = 600 km. Fuel needed for a full tank = 40 - 12 = 28 litres. Fill cost = 28 x 100 = 2,800. Tank level = (12 / 40) x 100 = 30.0%. So the driver can go 180 km now, and a full tank costs 2,800.
